{name}, you're still bloated after your visit. Your provider ordered a SIBO breath test — you've taken it and you're waiting — and they suggested Pepcid in the meantime. You're wondering about Genesis Gold.

Pepcid (famotidine) reduces stomach acid and is sometimes used for stomach distress. I don't want to contradict your healthcare provider, but I don't usually start with H2 blockers for possible SIBO. We want to protect your ability to digest and absorb nutrients, and stomach acid is part of that. What we need is to learn what's going on in the small intestine. Pepcid may ease symptoms until results return, but it isn't necessarily a treatment for overgrowth.

{name}, you've been trying to get a pediatrician visit and an education evaluation while your child struggles in school. You're not even sure of the diagnosis yet, and meanwhile you're sad for him and frustrated you can't get help. You're sleeping poorly and stress eating — and you haven't been practicing CALM.
Imaging and surgical planning belong with her specialist — bring the questions above to that visit.

This pattern fits what we often see with SIBO, but only a breath test with your provider can show whether overgrowth is there and what type. I'm recommending you bring these concerns to your healthcare provider and ask about a SIBO breath test.

The three suggestion chips under “How are you feeling today?” are different demo stories — tap them one by one to walk a real chat, then follow into Visit Notes after an answer. Typing free text works too. From here you can also open My Health, My Notes, labs, or the Wellness Plan card when one exists.

A first-time user has just opened the app. This is a short brand moment, about 3 seconds, while the app 'loads'. It should feel calm and trustworthy. It fades into Welcome. Returning users who already consented skip it and land in Main.
Welcome

Maria meets the Oracle for the first time. The aim is a warm, human first contact that asks only for her first name and makes clear she is talking to an AI. Get started accepts the terms and opens her first conversation. Sign in is there for returning users.

This is a calm, easy-to-scan summary of what the app is and isn't, plus the AI disclosure and the agreement checkbox. It was merged into Welcome on 2026-10-08, so it stays in the code but is no longer part of the flow. Agreeing opens the empty Conversation.

This is the consultation. Suggestions and replies drive a scripted flow: light intake, then the Oracle’s answer, then What’s next. From What’s next you can open the Wellness Plan, upload labs, or move into Visit Notes. Try one Home suggestion all the way through to see the full path.

Maria tapped a product from an answer, her 90-day plan or a piece of content. A mock Genesis Gold page opens in an in-app browser, labelled 'Formulated by Genesis Health Products', with ?ref=app. Shopping is a demo and checkout happens on the real site. Done takes her back to exactly where she was.

This sheet appears right after Maria's first completed answer. The Oracle offers to check in later so they can build on today. Maria picks a reminder interval. Our own friendly prompt always comes before the system permission alert. Not now dismisses it without any pressure.

Maria has used her 3 free consultations and is trying to start a new one. The sheet tells her that her answers are saved and invites her to choose a plan. It should never feel like a trap: safety features keep working. It leads to Choose plan, or Maybe later.
Choose plan

Maria compares the Individual and Family plans, either monthly or annually. One plan is always preselected based on where she came from (for example, Family when she came from the upgrade sheet). Continue takes her to account creation if she has no account yet, or straight to payment.

The account is created only at conversion, framed as 'Save your health history'. Maria can sign up with Apple, Google or email plus a verification code, and her trial history moves with her. In sign-in mode, opened from Welcome, it greets a returning user and takes them back to Main.
Plan success

The purchase is done. 'You're all set': unlimited consultations are unlocked and the trial counter disappears. Continue my conversation sends any message she had held back. Family plan users can go straight to adding a family member.

This is a mock of the App Store subscription sheet that confirms the plan, price and auto-renewal. It should feel familiar and trustworthy. Subscribe shows a short spinner, then Done, and moves on to the success screen. Cancel returns to Choose plan.

Weeks later, the Oracle reaches out with a generic nudge: 'How are you feeling this week?'. The lock screen never shows health details. Tapping it unlocks the phone and deep-links into a check-in conversation for the right profile. It is the moment that brings Maria back.
Upload or enter labs here (photo, PDF, or typed values). You’ll confirm the numbers on the next screen; the Oracle can then use them in chat. This is simulated reading — not real OCR.
Profile switcher

'Who is this for?' Maria can switch between herself and her family members, and each person keeps their own private history. Switching resets Ask and My Health to that person. From here she can add a member (or see the upgrade sheet if she isn't on the Family plan) or manage profiles.

Maria adds someone, for example her teen daughter, with their name, relationship, date of birth, sex at birth and a consent confirmation. Children under 13 are blocked for now. Create profile switches to the new person and opens an empty conversation with teen-appropriate suggestions.

Maria tried to add a family member but isn't on the Family plan. This light sheet explains that the plan covers up to 5 people, each with their own private history. Upgrade opens Choose plan with Family preselected, then returns her to adding the member. Not now dismisses it.
Profile details

This shows one person's basics and the health info gathered from intake, all editable, with links to their consultations, Visit Notes and labs. For profiles other than Maria's own, there is also a clearly destructive delete option. It reassures her that each profile's data is separate and under her control.

The Oracle's library

Maria can browse all of the Oracle's content: search it, filter by For you, All or New, or by topic. Empty results gently send her to ask the Oracle directly. This screen also links to the Facebook community and to About the Oracle.
About the Oracle

This screen explains what Oracle is: an AI system for health education and encouragement, what it can and can’t do, and who makes it. No person, portrait, books or credentials (legal change requests, Oct 26). Copy is placeholder until legal approves it.

When the app isn't enough, Maria can reach the support team herself. This screen explains what to expect from the 50-minute video visit, asks which state she lives in (for licensing) and offers an opt-in to share her app history. Choose a time leads to the scheduler. The price is still to be decided.

'Booked with the Oracle', with the date, time and a promise of a reminder the day before. Maria should feel looked after. She can add the visit to her calendar, view details (with a cancel option) or go back to chat. The booking also appears in her hub.

Maria rereads a past consultation: the transcript, the collapsed intake summary and the Oracle's full 7-section answer. She can download a PDF to bring to her provider, share it, or continue the chat, which reopens that conversation and the Oracle remembers it.

My Visit Notes

Log your visit

This is one calm place for Maria's plan, family profiles, notifications, privacy, legal and About the Oracle. Trial users see a Choose a plan card at the top. Sign out keeps her data in her account and returns her to Welcome.

This is where Maria exercises her data rights: download her data, read how it is used (never for training without consent), delete a profile, or delete her account. Deleting the account takes deliberate steps, including typing DELETE, and then resets the app. It should feel transparent and respectful.
This shows Maria's current plan, price and renewal date. She can change plan, manage it in the App Store, or cancel; the plan stays active until the renewal date. It isn't in the wireframes.

Maria controls check-in reminders (and how often they come) and booking reminders. A note reassures her that health details never show on her lock screen. If system permission is off, a banner offers a way to fix it. It isn't in the wireframes.
